entry.dc:title: Phytomining
entry.dc:creator: Brooks R.R.
entry.dc:description: Phytomining is the production of a 'crop' of a metal by growing high-biomass plants that accumulate high metal concentrations. Some of these plants are natural hyperaccumulators, and in others the property can be induced. Pioneering experiments in this field might lead to a 'green' alternative to existing, environmentally destructive, opencast mining practices. Phytomining for a range of metals is a real possibility, with the additional potential of the exploitation of ore bodies that it is uneconomic to mine by conventional methods.

entry.dc:title: Standardization of machines and belt conveyor systems of brown coal surface mining
entry.dc:creator: Eickemeier J.
entry.dc:description: With the introduction of the EC Machine Regulation on the 9th Ordinance Implementing the Law on Equipment Safety, the brown coal mining industry found it necessary to draw up standard specifications for opencast mining machines and belt conveyor systems. Hitherto, these had been erected in accordance with the development plan licensing procedure, which for the most part was based on regulations issued by the State Mines Inspectorate. These specifications contained in these basic regulations were included in the new standards and adapted to the present state of the art.

entry.dc:title: Opencast mining of coal in high flood level zone of River Godavari - a case study
entry.dc:creator: Vanam G.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: The Medapalli opencast mine of Singareni Collieries Company Limited is situated on the right bank of River Godavari and 90% of the mine area falls within the high flood level (HFL) zone of the river. With the total of seven coal seams, the mine is forecasted to produce 1.25 million tons annually. The mine will supply coal mainly to powerhouses.

entry.dc:title: Development, present state and future prospects of continuous combined cross-pit dumping in surface mining
entry.dc:creator: Drebenstedt C.
entry.prism:publicationName: Prace Naukowe Instytutu Gornictwa Politechniki Wroclawskiej
entry.dc:description: The most favourable variant of overburden removal in opencast mining is direct dumping of the overburden without the use of haulage means and by the shortest route over the raw material and onto the open floor. Cross-pit dumping combinations, each consisting of a continuously excavating and dumping machine with interconnected operation, have been used for the past 100 years for this economical variant of overburden removal. After first having been applied in Germany, this technique and technology began to used worldwide in the late 1950s. Since then, bucket wheel excavator and spreader combinations in particular, which nowadays achieve a cutting height of up to 30 m and a yearly output of 20 Mm<sup>3</sup>, are used effectively as a rule in the lower overburden section or to remove intermediate rock. As far as an extension of the scope of oreration of cross-pit dumping combinations is concerned, there are a number of technical and technological solutions available which make an effective exploitation of small or geologically complex deposits possible.

entry.dc:title: Modernisation as method of service time extension of aged surface mining machines
entry.dc:creator: Kowalczyk M.
entry.prism:publicationName: Prace Naukowe Instytutu Gornictwa Politechniki Wroclawskiej
entry.dc:description: All the basic opencast mining machines operating in Polish open pits have been listed with their service time indicated. The paper presents a method of estimating reserves of service time in these machines. The current state of technology and exploitation of opencast mining machines is outlined. Basic technological reasons for the modernisation of the steel structures are given and some modernisation designs made by the SKW firm are described. The paper also presents the economic side of such undertakings on the basis of the authors' own experience acquired during the reconstruction and modernisation of aged machines.

entry.dc:title: Land-use mapping and change detection in a coal mining area - A case study in the Jharia coalfield, India
entry.dc:creator: Prakash A.
entry.dc:description: In an area like the Jharia coalfield (JCF), where extensive and rapid underground and opencast mining is going on continuously, land-use studies are of paramount importance. This paper discusses the remote sensing-GIS techniques used for identification of various land-use classes on satellite imagery and enhanced products and identification of time-sequential changes in land-use patterns. The various land-use classes, recognised from satellite image data and field surveys, are dense vegetation, sparse vegetation, fire, opencast mining (coal), overburden dump, subsidence and barren wasteland, settlement, transport network, river and water pond. A number of image processing operations have been carried out on remote sensing data for enhancing land-use patterns. It has been found that Landsat TM false colour composites (FCC) of bands 4, 3 and 2; FCC of bands 7, 5 and 3; FCC of bands 5, 4 and 2 and ratio images provide very useful information for land-use mapping. The normalised difference vegetation index (NDVI) images have been used for vegetation studies. Image characters of various land-use classes on black-and-white and enhanced colour products have been tabulated. Land-use maps of selected windows have been prepared and examples given. Time-sequential surface changes that have occurred in the JCF since 1975 and particularly between November 1990 to November 1994 have been investigated. For change detection analysis, data manipulation in several steps involving preprocessing, processing and colour display have been carried out. Land-use changes have been detected by (a) image differencing, (b) image ratioing, and (c) differencing of NDVI images. It is inferred from the remote sensing images that extensive mining, establishment of communication networks, expansion of settlements, decrease in the vegetation cover etc., have remodelled the face of the JCF. © 1998, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. entry.dc:title: Ecologically compatible and energy-saving aerostatic rope haulage systems for transport tasks
entry.dc:creator: Butkin V.
entry.dc:description: The paper describes a rope haulage system that makes use of the aerostatic buoyancy of captive balloons. By applying the captive balloon technique it is possible to construct rope haulage systems of less complicated design and to make rope haulage far more economical. The basic function of aerostatic rope haulage systems is described in detail. There is a wide scope for application of this technique. Opencast mining in mountainous regions is, however, regarded as its main field of application. Building projects and agriculture also offer scope for this technique. Its use in mining ranges from output haulage and overburden removal to dumping. Moreover, with the aid of the aerostatic rope haulage system the problem of ventilation in deep and narrow opencast mines can be solved.

entry.dc:title: Benches - haul roads - berms and spoil heaps in opencast mining
entry.dc:creator: Mishra M.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: Proper design of working benches, haul roads, berms, spoil heaps and drainage arrangement and their proper upkeep is important in an opencast mine in terms of productivity, cost-effectiveness and safety. The overall mine dimensions must be precisely established before the design of individual benches, roadways and spoil heaps. The following major factors determine these dimensions: strike and dip of the seams; outcrop/incrop position; seam thickness; stratigraphy; layout flexibility; drainage requirement; haul distance; ramp locations; rainfall; and land use plan.

entry.dc:title: Energy - motor and problem area of development
entry.dc:description: The article examines the problem of energy, which is at the same time a key factor in development and an environmental problem the link between living standards and energy is explored, and the energy policies of Europe and Germany are examined. The role of brown coal in the energy market is noted, and the relative importance of brown coal in the eastern and western parts of Germany is compared. The development of brown coal fields of Germany - Rhineland (Rheinisch), Central Germany (Mitteldeutsch), Helmstedt and Lausitz by opencast mining is analysed. New power station technologies are outlined, and the problem of energy and the environment is discussed.

entry.dc:title: Orgreave reclamation and landfill containment void, Sheffield
entry.dc:creator: Smithson J.
entry.prism:publicationName: Geoenvironmental Engineering Contaminated Ground Fate of Pollutants and Remediation Proc Conference Cardiff 1997
entry.dc:description: Orgreave Reclamation Site is located within the Orgreave Open Cast Coal Site in the administrative boundary of Rotherham, South Yorkshire. The 256ha site was dominated by the former Orgreave coking plant and colliery. The coking plant, colliery and associated chemical works closed down in the early 1990s and have subsequently been demolished. The site is now owned and operated by RJB Mining (UK) Ltd for coal extraction by opencast mining. Extensive ground contamination has required major remediation works and the development of an on-site containment void to release that part of the site for opencast working.

entry.dc:title: Monitoring of induced seismicity in Albania
entry.dc:creator: Muco B.
entry.prism:publicationName: Engineering Geology and the Environment Proc Symposium Athens 1997 Vol 1
entry.dc:description: It is well known that the man with the design and construction of large engineering works and schemes, can influence on various environmental aspects. Geomorphic, seismological and environmental changes during the filling up and operation of large reservoirs are evidenced world-wide. There are also many reports for the above mentioned changes which are connected with underground nuclear tests, blast in mines and opencast mining and other large explosions. Lastly, those changes could be induced also by oil and gas extraction. The so-called induced seismicity developed mostly at last three decades, is a very interesting seismological field to be studied even from engineering geology and environment point of view. Monitoring the induced seismicity in Albania during the last 20 years, in this paper there are evidenced cases of induced seismic activity caused by large reservoirs, blasts carried in various mines and oil extraction.

entry.dc:title: Siemens involvement in opencast mining
entry.dc:creator: Varma S.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: This paper aims to highlights some of the requirements for opencast mining electricals as well as the involvement of Siemens in few major projects. It is shown that the experiences of Siemens in understanding these requirements in terms of engineering, supply, installation, testing and commissioning including project management are manifested in the large projects executed for different equipment at various sites with diverse technology as per clients needs.

entry.dc:title: Applicable criteria of plant engineering in Lusatian opencast mines with conveying bridges
entry.dc:creator: Haege K.
entry.dc:description: During the past years, the scope of plant engineering in the opencast mines of Lusatia has been widened considerably. The number of machines and the variety of types were adapted to the different tasks and to the requirements for a high reliability of supply to power stations and briquetting plants. This resulted in a considerable cost burden. By outsourcing tasks connected with the accessory processes of opencast mining, concentration on the main processes, excavation, transport and dumping of overburden coal, as well as on the repair work and shifting operations connected with these processes were achieved. Coping with this wide range of tasks has been possible through the setting up of a new division, `Mining Operation and Process Planning'.

entry.dc:title: Constructional and technical operational preconditions and practical results when developing a surface miner for service in Russian opencast mines
entry.dc:creator: Saprykin J.
entry.dc:description: An industrial prototype of the Continuous Surface Miner, type 2000R, for slicewise stripping with a wide receiving element, which is adapted to the climatic and mining conditions in the Russian opencast mining areas where it is to be used, i.e. in the Kuznetsk Basin was developed. This machine, with a compressive strength of 20 to 70 MPa and a friability coefficient of 7 to 10, is suitable mainly for overburden removal (aleurolith, argillite and sandstone). The digging element of the machine, with gravity discharge, has a diameter of 4.8 m and 4 digging wheels. The machine is equipped with 400 rotary bits. Proof of the efficiency of this machine having been established, it is now being tried out in an endurance test under operating conditions in the Taldynskij open-cast mine (Kusbas region). It is used in cyclic operation in combination with heavy-duty trucks with a carrying capacity of 110 t.

entry.dc:title: Possible uses of surface miners and first operating results in hard rock
entry.dc:creator: Spachtholz F.
entry.dc:description: The concept of a non-explosive excavation technique for opencast mining in hard rock is described with the aim of extending the applicability of this technique to zones of rock with greater hardness. In this connection, the most favourable mechanical principle of the forces to be induced centrally between the front and rear travel gear set is considered. On the basis of the requirements of this new excavation technique which were determining from the operating experience gained with the SM 2100 EX, the concept of the DSM, an excavating machine for hard rock opencast mining equipped with individual discs and a receiving drum cutter, is evolved and the possible economic advantages are set forth. These considerations represent a further step towards replacing drilling and blasting processes by a continuously operating system in opencast mining in hard rock.

entry.dc:title: Respiratory health effects of opencast coalmining: A cross sectional study of current workers
entry.dc:creator: Love R.G.
entry.dc:description: Objectives-To identify whether there is evidence of pneumoconiosis and other respiratory health effects associated with exposure to respirable mixed dust and quartz in United Kingdom opencast coalmines. Methods-A cross sectional study of current workers (1224 men, 25 women) was carried out at nine large and medium sized opencast sites in England, Scotland, and Wales. To characterise a range of occupational groups within the industry, full shift measurements of personal exposures to respirable dust and quartz were taken. Up to three surveys were carried out at each site, covering all four seasons. For the purposes of comparisons with health indices these groups were further condensed into five broad combined occupational groups. Full sized chest radiographs, respiratory symptoms, occupational history questionnaires, and simple spirometry were used to characterise the respiratory health of the workforce. Logistic or multiple regression techniques were used to examine relations between indices of exposure and respiratory health. Results-None of the group geometric mean dust concentrations, based on 626 valid dust samples, exceeded 1 mg.m<sup>-3</sup>, and 99% of all quartz concentrations were below 0.4 mg.m<sup>-3</sup>, the current maximum exposure limit. The highest quartz concentrations were experienced by the rock drilling team and drivers of bulldozers (used to move earth and stone from layers of coal). There were clear differences in mean respirable dust and quartz concentrations between occupational groups. These were consistent across the different sites, but depended in part on the day of measurement. The variations between sites were not much greater than between days, suggesting that differences between sites were at least partly explained by differences in conditions at the time of the measurements. The prevalence of radiographic small opacities profusion category ≤ 1/0, based on the median of three readings, was 4.4%. Five men had category 2 pneumoconiosis and two men (including one of these five) had progressive massive fibrosis category A. From regression analyses, the relative risk of attaining a profusion of category ≤ 0/1 was estimated to be doubled for every 10 years worked in the dustiest, preproduction opencast jobs, after allowing for age, smoking, and site effects. Risk was not associated with time worked in any other occupation within the industry, nor with previous employment in underground mining or other dusty jobs. Symptoms of chronic bronchitis were present in 13% of the men. Frequency of chronic bronchitis was influenced by years worked in dusty jobs outside opencast mining, but not by time spent in occupations within the industry. Asthmatic symptoms were reported by 5% of the workforce, close to the mean frequency found in adult men. No positive associations were found between asthma and occupational exposures. Lung function on average was close to predicted values and showed no relation to time worked in opencast occupations. Conclusions-Frequency of (mostly mild) chest radiographic abnormalities is associated with working in the dustier, prepreduction jobs in the industry. Although some of these mild abnormalities may be non-occupational (due to aging or smoking), the association with exposure indicates a small risk of pneumoconiosis in these men, and the need to monitor and control exposures, particularly in the high risk occupations.

entry.dc:title: Textural and mineralogical characteristics of SPM in coal mines
entry.dc:creator: Jamal A.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
entry.dc:description: The ultimate goal of air pollution assessment and control effort is to mitigate the effect of pollutants on environment. The effects may be on health, various other biological and systems, and physical quality of environnent. The severity of impact of airborned suspended particulate matter nay depends upon its physico-chemical properties. Opencast mining operation often generates high percentage of airborned Suspended Particulate Matter (SPM) which gets dissipated into the atmosphere around the mine and leads to serious disruption to the quality of the life. To this paper, a study of air quality monitoring in terms of SPM in an opencast coal mine has been presented. Among the various mining activities drilling, coal crushing and handling operations and movement of dumpers on the haul roads are the main sources of dust generation in an opencast coalmine. The concentration of SPM is variable throughout the year. It shows wide variation in summer and winter seasons in mining area. The mineral constituents present in the SPM also vary considerably.

entry.dc:title: Restoration of the Ackton opencast coal site, West Yorkshire
entry.prism:publicationName: Coal International Mining and Quarry World
entry.dc:description: This short article describes the restoration of a site which was scarred by spoil heaps from underground mining and from subsequent opencast mining operations. The reinstatement of the site resulted in a prestigious environmental award for Miller Mining.

entry.dc:title: Coal geology, chemical and petrographical characteristics, and implications for coalbed methane development of subbituminous coals from the Sorgun and Suluova Eocene basins, Turkey
entry.dc:creator: Karayigit A.I.
entry.dc:description: The Sorgun and Suluova basins contain a thick and laterally extensive Lower Eocene coal seam. The stratigraphy of both basins comprises basement rocks, the Yozgat Granitoid of Pre-Eocene age in the Sorgun basin and Jurassic-Cretaceous limestones in the Suluova basin, overlain unconformably by the coal-bearing Lower Eocene Celtek Formation and by transgressive units of Middle-Upper Eocene age. In the Sorgun basin the Artova Ophiolitic Complex tectonically overlies the transgressive units. Neogene and Quaternary deposits cover all the older units unconformably in both basins. The single coal seam is located at the base of the Celtek Formation and reaches a thickness of 6 m in the open-cast mine at Sorgun and 8 m in boreholes in the Suluova basin. Some coal is produced by opencast mining, but most is produced by underground mining methods. A total of 75 coal samples was collected from both basins and analysed chemically and petrographically. The coals are characterized by a relatively low moisture content (0.7-9.3 wt% on an air-dried basis) and variable ash yields (2.4-67.8 wt% on an air-dried basis) and huminite contents (28.4-89.6 vol%). Measurements of the mean random reflectance of ulminite (mainly eu-ulminite A) vary between 0.46 and 0.60% (0.53% average). These reflectance values and the chemical analyses show that the rank is subbituminous A or transitional to high-volatile bituminous C coal according to the ASTM classification. The coalbed methane potential of both basins is at present unknown. No borehole has been drilled to explore for this resource and no gas capacity value has been obtained for the coal seam and bituminous shales. The methane explosions which have occurred during coal production in the underground mines imply that both basins may have been an important potential for coalbed methane.

entry.dc:title: Variation in the concentration of heavy metal contents in minespoil dumps and its relation to vegetational establishments
entry.dc:creator: Pandya S.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Surface Science and Technology
entry.dc:description: With a view to utilisation of enormous minespoil dumps from increasing opencast mining, for vegetational establishments, characterisation of these materials have been undertaken with special reference to nutrients and heavy metals. Pb, Mn, Fe, Cu, Co, Ni, Cr, B and Cd in the soil and also in the grains of 13 different crops in different seasons have been determined before and after cropping using an Atomic Absorption Spectrophotometer. Addition of ameliorating material, i.e., lime sludge from pulp and papermills have shown interesting results in the stabilisation of overburden material for cropping. © 1996 Indian Society for Surface Science and Technology,.

entry.dc:title: Flooding concept for the residual holes of opencast mining
entry.dc:creator: Luckner L.
entry.dc:description: Reclaiming of the water resource systems in the mining regions of Lausitz (Lusatian) area of the former East Germany required flooding of the remaining opencast lignite mines which finished their production after the reunification of Germany. This flooding was regarded as a transient state between achieve mining and a restored land scape which follows mining. A number of urgent decisions had to be taken, as each day's delay meant further acidification of the water. This shown that overcoming water shortages in the area under discussion caused by groundwater mismanagement over decades requires region-wide management of groundwater and surface water resources.

entry.dc:title: Rational exploitation of non-renewable resources through opencast mining for a fast expanding Indian cement industry vis-a-vis sustainable development
entry.dc:creator: Paul P.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: India is blessed with considerable mineral endowment which, if utilized in optimal manner can go a long way in accelerating industrial growth and thereby the economic development of the country. Minerals and mineral based industries, namely steel, cement and many others have been one of the major contributors for the progress of a country. Sustainable growth of the mining of the raw materials in the mineral sector is closely linked with rational exploitation through advanced techniques keeping in view environmental aspects as well. The present paper highlights state-of-the art of the opencast mining techniques which would rationalize the mineral exploitation and also bring in the much-needed mineral conservation. The magnitude and significance of the environmental degradation caused by opencast mining with proper abatement measures have also been discussed.

entry.dc:title: Making the solution stick
entry.dc:description: In the former Soviet Union, productivity at mines is hit hard by the sticking and freezing of coal to the surfaces of chutes and bunkers, and the loss of coal during transportation. For some years now NIIOGR, a Russian opencast mining research institute, has been studying the use of polymer compositions to prevent such things happening.

entry.dc:title: Mapping geological features of the Jharia coalfield from Landsat-5 TM data
entry.dc:creator: Chatterjee R.S.
entry.dc:description: False Colour Composite 754, the principal component imagery and edge enhanced imagery of Landsat-5 TM data have been found useful in delineating the regional geological features, viz, the curvilinear coal bands and sandstone ridges, faults, fractures and dolerite dykes of the Jharia Coalfield of Bihar, India, covering an area of about 480 km<sup>2</sup>, where many parts are inaccessible to direct field mapping due to extensive opencast mining operations. The features, their occurrences and spatial dispositions, as deciphered from satellite data, are found to match significantly well with selective field maps. © 1996 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
